answer: Bind each agent seat to a limited-entry commercial fishing permit. A state fishery agency caps the permits for each inlet, ties every permit to one named skipper and a registered vessel, and audits landing tickets each season. Because permits trade openly, their price is public and often tops $100,000, so a sybil farm wanting 200 seats would need over $20M in permits. A glacier-fed inlet behind a basalt breakwater simply has no berths for phantom boats.
